name: Ukdah
description: A star 81 parsecs away, 30 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 47431: radius 29.544 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 270.611 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.059) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 47431: effective temperature 4310 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.066)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 1.78 from 2024A&A...682A.145S; the 14 published values span log g 1.31 to 2.35, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 47431: distance 80.71 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.011), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 81 parsecs away, 30 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 271 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,310 K, so 29.544 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 47431: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Iota Hydrae
quotes.card: Iota Hydrae, formally named Ukdah, is a star in the constellation of Hydra, about 8° to the north-northwest of Alphard and just to the south of the celestial equator.
quotes.introduction: Visible to the naked eye, it is a suspected variable star with an apparent visual magnitude that ranges between 3.87 and 3.91.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 3827873938815011200 (quality A), from 2008AJ....135..209M; Gaia DR3 measures none
